_doc: Player-facing changelog, newest first. The lead appends an entry at each publish (from the feedback reports' Completed notes). `id` is stable; the client remembers the last id a player has seen and highlights newer ones. Plain language, no internal names.

entries.title: Sign in with your phone, class armour, and tidier characters
items: Sign in with your phone: on a PC or console, choose Log in, then "Sign in with your phone (QR code)". Scan the code, log in on your phone (your password manager can fill it in), check the code matches, and tap Yes — the other screen signs in. Your password is never typed on the big screen.
Every calling now starts in its own armour. You still choose your starting weapons, and no two choices show the same weapons any more.
Characters look tidier: glasses have proper rectangular frames, hair and hats no longer show gaps, blades meet their hilts, and many clothes, straps and helmets no longer let you see through them.
Armour takes the colour of your top, short capes sit over broad shoulders, and giants and halflings are better proportioned.

entries.title: A new Torbor Downs, achievements, a new character screen, and fixes from your reports
items: Torbor Downs is rebuilt: more hills and valleys, real coastlines where the land meets the sea, and a dozen named regions with their own ground, trees and grass. Every road, town and dungeon is where it was, and if you logged out somewhere that changed, you wake on good ground nearby.

Achievements and trophies: press Y. Many pay gold or a gift box by post. Help bring down a world boss or break a siege for a trophy, and be the first in the realm to do something for a Realm First that everyone hears about.
Link items, achievements and trophies in chat: Shift-click an item while you are typing, or press Link in the Achievements window.
A new character screen: the calling is chosen from cards showing every skill, the name box starts empty, and a taken name is said straight away instead of signing you in.
Towns now say how big they are (hamlet, village, town, city), every city has every shop, and the ox-cart window shows each stop's size and who works there.
New two-handed polearms: the Glaive and the Bardiche. Two spears now take turns, and every lightning bolt looks like lightning. Storm Orbs circle you.

Fixed: "Not while you are fighting" with nothing near you; the Brineglass Tubes dropping you on the corner of the sea (and /reset, or Stuck? in the menu, if you ever get stuck); boss rewards waiting on a body that was gone (they go to your bag now, with a reward card); the same event announced again at every zone; the damage meter reopening at log-in.

Also: your map arrow turns with you and the map works better on phones; a barrier shows on your health bar; guards come to help; a controller test in Settings; class descriptions match the real skills; trees look like storybook trees up close; new grass for every kind of ground.
On a phone, typing in chat no longer closes the keyboard after the first letter.

On phones, the Fish button shows again when you have a rod, and Fish (that button, the quick wheel, X on a keyboard, hold LT + A on a controller) casts a line again; both had stopped working when fishing moved to fishing spots.
On a slow phone the quick wheel no longer closes the moment it opens.

entries.title: Fairer fights, no more freezes, and lots of fixes from your reports
items: Fixed the freezes during fights with spellcasting and shooting enemies, including ashback salamanders: their spell effects no longer rebuild their graphics every cast, and an area spell at your feet appears without a lock-up so you can step out in time.
Enemy arrows and spells no longer follow you. Keep moving and you can dodge most of them.
Enemies now run after you when you try to get away, and some sprint. Attacking while moving slows you, so stop attacking to escape.
Scattered Stars fires its stars one after another, like a volley. Starlight orbs only show over your own character and sit behind your shoulders instead of spinning like a daze.
Damage numbers that land at the same time spread apart so you can read each one.
Set pieces now show their set on the item card: how many pieces you wear and what each step gives, ticked when it's on. The bonuses always applied; the card just never said so.
The sceptre's card now says plainly that it only hits what's in reach and doesn't shoot.
Bulk skinning: press E on one of your kills and you skin every beast of yours within 10 m, one after another. Escape stops.
Bug reports can attach a screenshot, with an option to hide the interface.
Sign in on your phone with a QR code: Account, then 'Sign in on your phone'. The code works once, for 3 minutes, and never holds your password.
Selling a rare item asks once more, with 'Remember for this transaction' so that trader stops asking until you leave.
Controllers reach every key of the on-screen keyboard, and on wide screens like the Steam Deck the keyboard is wide and low with its own Delete, Capitals, Space and Send keys.
Perk search only lights perks whose own name or description has the word. On a phone, tap a perk to read it, and tap again to stage it.
On small screens, character creation scrolls so Next is always reachable, and the logo steps aside while you customise your look.
Swimming forward is a face-down front crawl, and treading water is upright. Sitting, eating and riding a cart sit down once and stay seated. When you fish, you turn to face the float.
No more dark seams in the sea while sailing, and the ship comes alongside gently instead of whipping round on arrival.
Folk standing at a town's edge, like Mistfall's carter, can be seen from inside and outside the town.
Fences and walls built in rings (watchtower yards, ruined forts, animal pens, Vharlen's goat walls) follow the ring instead of sticking out like spokes. The blindfold is gone from every face.
The ground looks better: grass, ferns, heather, stones and pebbles on the ground everywhere, a matte earth that no longer shines, and taller palm trees on Vharlen.
Want to know what's coming? There's a new To-do list link on the title screen and in What's new.

entries.title: A layout for controllers (Steam Deck and gamepads)
items: Pick up a controller and the screen switches to a controller layout by itself: the menu bar goes, the chat folds down to its last few lines (which fade), and your quests and events fold to one line under the map, so you see the world instead of panels. Use the mouse or keyboard again and it switches back.

Menu (Start) now opens a big menu with every window: bag, character, skills, perks, journal, map, party, friends, guild, mail, market, group finder, chat, settings, controls, what's new, feedback, account and log out. Move with the stick or D-pad, A opens, B goes back.
Every window works with the controller: LB and RB change tabs, the right stick scrolls, Y shows an item's card. View opens the map.
Hold LT and press View to chat (an on-screen keyboard opens). Hold LT and press Menu to show or fold your quest list.
Settings > Key bindings > Layout lets you keep the controller layout or the desktop one if you prefer.

entries.title: New faces: livelier characters and many more looks
items: Every character in the world has a new, more careful model: hair and hats fit properly, beards sit over the chest, and long robes, dresses and coats no longer have feet poking through them when you run.
Eyes blink now, and glance around when idle. People look at things: townsfolk turn their eyes to you as you walk up, enemies watch whoever they are fighting, and your character looks at your target.

Character creation and the barber have many more choices: 9 new eye shapes with pupil and iris styles and odd-coloured eyes, 10 new hairstyles (some with a second colour), new brows, mouths, noses, ear shapes that suit your people, 6 new beards and 10 new face marks.
New body options too: a body type (slim, athletic, broad, stocky, heavy, petite, lanky), posture, shoulder width, leg length and arm thickness.
Characters you already made look the way they did, on the new model, and can visit the barber to try the new options.

entries.title: Wandering packs and six new events: a wilder, more dangerous world
items: Packs of 5 to 10 monsters now roam the wilds instead of waiting at camps: hound hunts, boar sounders, hyena clans, brigand crews with archers, bone marches, cult processions, fen broods, and on the Burning Isle Slagborn war-parties, prowler packs and pumice processions. You meet one every couple of minutes on the roads.
Many are led by a named elite with a banner on its back and a line over its name. Bring the leader down and a beast pack scatters — or a pack that fights to the end turns savage and hits harder.
The whole pack comes when you pull one, and gives up together. Each member is weaker than a lone monster, so area spells shine. A pack grows tougher for every extra player fighting it.
A wiped pack leaves its spoils where it fell — a bundle only those who fought can open (a rare item if it had a leader) — plus a share of a level of experience.
Packs live their lives: brigands light a fire and sit round it, hounds and prowlers run down deer and goats and feed, cultists stand in a ring.

New events that come to you: an Ambush on the Road (both sides at once), a Caravan Under Attack (save the drover), a Night Raid on a village (its militia fight beside you), a Rift that spits monsters until you seal it three times, a Warlord marching a war-band across the zone, and Bounties on pack leaders with their last-seen spot on your map. Each has a tracker card, a map pin and a reward for everyone who helps.

entries.title: A prettier world: water, mist, light and lived-in towns
items: Water got a makeover: clear turquoise shallows, deep blue sea, glinting ripples and white surf rolling onto the shore, with foam round piers and rocks.
Soft mist drifts over the sea and down in the valleys, and cloud shadows slide across the land on sunny days. Warmer, softer light everywhere, and a glow round lamps and spells at night on High.

Towns look lived in: walls show their brick, stone, plaster and timber, roofs their tiles and thatch, and streets and squares have barrels, crates, sacks, benches and proper lanterns. Gullwick's quay and Port Vharl's beach have their own harbour clutter.
Monsters and townsfolk have painted portraits in the target frame; your own character still shows your look.
Settings → Graphics lists what Low, Medium and High draw. Phones start on Medium and run nearly as fast as before.
Several controllers: whichever one you touched last plays (a docked Steam Deck with a second pad works now). Swords swing with your arm when you run. Gullwick sits on its own bay with a real harbour.

entries.title: The Star Blade, the Market, and 60 of your reports
items: New class: the Star Blade, the Starcaller's partner in plate. It fights up close with a sword of starlight: a star shield that strikes back at melee blows, star threads that drag enemies in, and rings of stars that pin a crowd. It has its own talents, outfit, icons, spell effects and a class quest at the Nine Maidens. It fills Starlight from blows given and taken.

Player Market: a Market tab in the party window. List gear or materials at your own price for a small fee; listings last 30 days, can be cancelled, and everything arrives by mail. A full bag never loses a reward: it comes by mail instead.

Combat: weapon attacks are a third slower and every skill does twice the damage. Melee weapons take 10–15% off every hit you take. Rares and champions have far less health; a rare always drops at least a rare item.

Strength, Dexterity, Intellect and Constitution are gone. Their health, mana, crit and dodge are plain stats now, and each weapon shows its own damage bonus. Old items and perks were converted, so nobody lost anything.
Bosses no longer heal back to a full bar for a last phase. The Wand of the Ninth Star is arcane and really throws three stars.
Starcallers gain Starlight from level 6. Clearer Early Bond, magic find, gold find and experience descriptions.

Bag tabs: Equipment, Items and Other (Other never fills). Every character carries a recall charm that can't be lost or used up. The shop's Sell tab has Equipment and Items filters, and Shift-compare works everywhere.

Mounts: new characters buy a Trail Horse (120 gold) instead of getting one free. A Mount slot picks and compares your mounts, pricier mounts are faster, and saddle bags add 12 bag slots. Bigger horses. Vharlen sells two lizards: the Ash Strider and the Slag Basker.

Every character knows all ten professions and carries the tools. Profession experience ×3. A Fine or Perfect gathering game gives half as much again plus an uncommon find. Crafted gear is always magic with a good chance at rare, and is the weapon you picked.
Fishing happens at fishing spots: walk up to rippling water and press E. The action bar's fishing button is now a Mount button. Ash trees around the starting lands can be chopped at Logging 1.

Raids cover the whole town and grow with the number of players. Monsters chase you three times as far. Loot rolls fresh after a server restart. Kill quests have enough monsters for several players, and class quest steps stay close together.

Shrine and pilgrim-post blessings really work now and say exactly what they give. Townsfolk take turns talking. Carts leave along the road. Looted bodies can still be skinned with E but can't be clicked.

The world: a sky that changes with time, weather and place; denser forests with much taller trees; tree and rock collisions that fit the shapes; click-to-move walks around obstacles; archers shoot arrows; travel icons over harbourmasters and cart drivers; giants are giant.

Controller: attacking with no target picks the nearest enemy; item cards and compare in the bag; loot starts on the first item. The damage meter records from login and no longer loses a fight when you die. NPC greetings go to chat.

entries.title: Auto-attack keeps to your target, and you can shoot on the run
items: Your auto-attack only hits the enemy you selected. Before, a shot could land on whatever was nearest the line, and arrows splashed onto the small enemies standing next to a big one.
Keep attacking while you move: your character turns at the hips to face the target and keeps shooting or swinging at it, whichever way you run. Run straight away and you backpedal.
You can get 10 wrong passwords before an account locks for a few minutes (it was 5).
New "Create an account" link on the Log in tab: pick a username and password straight away instead of playing as a guest first. Add an email and a forgotten password can be reset by email.

entries.title: Expansion: Vharlen, the Burning Isle
items: Torbor Downs is now an island in its own right. The land falls away to the sea at its edges, and the map shows open sea where it used to show locked land.

New island for levels 10 to 20: Vharlen, a young volcano across the sea. Nine new zones: black-sand beaches, a steaming jungle, sulphur flats, mud fens, obsidian dunes, grey pumice wastes, a valley buried in ash, basalt ridges and the crater itself.

The only way there is by ship. Talk to Osric Fennimore, the Harbourmaster in Gullwick (60 gold), and sail the Saltwren across the open sea to Port Vharl. You stand on deck for the crossing and can skip it after a few seconds. Tavu Okkarin sails you back. A level 8 quest in Gullwick, Smoke on the Horizon, sends you on your first voyage.

The Vharl live in stilt houses of dark basalt and red plaster. Their towns, people, shops and quests are all new: 54 quests, 18 rares, 9 elites, zone events, eight new dungeons and a world boss, Ossathra the Caldera Wyrm.

New monsters found only on the island: Scoria Crawlers, Ashback Salamanders, Pumice Golems, Vent Wisps, Glasswings, Steamwood Prowlers, Sulphur Toads, Obsidian Wardens, Mudback Lurkers and the Slagborn raiders.
Hot springs: rest in one out of combat to get health and mana back fast, and climb out Steam-warmed (+5% maximum health for 10 minutes).
Geysers rumble, then erupt. Stand on one and it throws you high into the air so you can drift down onto ledges. Monsters get thrown too.
Lava vents glow, warn you, then spout fire along the crack. They hurt, and monsters burn in them too.
Ash falls in the Pumice Wastes and Ashfall Hollow and shortens how far you can see.
New materials to gather (obsidian, sulphur, ironpalm, steamcap, cinderbloom and salamander hide), new recipes, 15 new fish and 9 new legendary catches.

entries.title: New icons everywhere, and every class's spells have their own look
items: Every icon that was a plain drawing is now a proper picture: the Attack and Cast a line buttons, the window buttons, emotes, professions, and in your bag every potion, meal, tool, material and fish. The Mana Potion is blue now.
Armour and clothing icons are shown on a plain shop mannequin instead of a stranger.

Each of the 30 classes now has its own spell effects on top of the element ones: its own shapes, colours and movement. A bard's spells throw music notes, a tinker's throw cogs, a chronomancer's lay down a ticking clock face, and so on.
New setting: Settings, Graphics, Spell effects. Enhanced, Standard, Reduced (full effects only for your own spells and your target) or Off (only projectiles). It applies at once.

entries.title: Cheaper gear, Starcaller, emotes and the last of your reports
items: Gear in shops costs about a fifth of what it did: expect to afford an uncommon piece every 20 to 30 minutes of play and a rare every hour and a half to two hours.

Potions, food, rods, bait, backpacks, mounts and waystone travel are all cheaper; a healing potion is 10 gold and the first horse is 400. Merchants pay 6% of an item's price instead of 1.2%, so a sold drop is worth about the same gold as before.

New class: the Starcaller, an arcane caster in midnight-blue robes with gold trim. Golden stars fly from your hand, bigger ones streak down from the sky and land with a ring of light, Star Field is a glowing star rune on the ground, and your Starlight circles your head as small gold motes. It has its own class quest, "Nine Stones, Nine Stars".
Spell bolts and arrows are now visible in flight for everyone nearby, from every class and every monster. Before, most of them were never sent to other players.

Hands have rules now: "Main hand" and "Off hand" items fit only that hand, "One-hand" fits either. Wands and tomes are the casters' attacking weapons; orbs are off-hand tools that change your basic attack. Weapons show their attacks per second.
/wave, /sit, /dance, /cheer, /bow and /point play on your character for everyone who can see you, and you wave while calling your mount.
Storm Beam is a constant crackling beam that flares with each pulse. Blessed Earth with Moving Light (and other carried zones) visibly follows you.
When an enemy is knocked back mid wind-up its warning area moves with it, and an interrupted attack's warning disappears at once. Enemies in dungeons can no longer hit you through walls.
A looted corpse can no longer be clicked or Tab-targeted, and a live enemy always wins over a corpse under your cursor. Stun stars no longer hang over a dead enemy.
Looting several bodies that lie together no longer leaves the loot window stuck open: it closes when everything is taken, or moves on to the next body in reach.
Enemies take 90 to 150 seconds to come back, and never within a minute where their killer is standing.
Every town and city has training dummies near its square, and they are proper straw dummies on a post now, not dogs.

Guards, scouts, hunters, road patrols and caravan guards out in the wilds fight monsters that come near them while you are close by. Help one win and they thank you, sometimes with gold and rarely with an item.
You can skin anything with an animal's body, including Barrow Hounds and the beast bosses. When a monster cannot be skinned the game says why.
Trade mini-games wait for you: skinning starts when your mouse reaches the knife, and nothing starts by itself. The forge no longer says it is "warming up".
The angler has the same trades button and trainer window as every other teacher. The prospector's title is just "Prospector".
When an item mentions a status such as Cursed, Burning or Poisoned, the bottom of its card explains what that status does.
Signing in on a browser that holds guest characters now offers to move them onto your account.
Settings has a new switch, "Let friends see where I am". Typing /meter after closing the damage meter brings it straight back.
Ordinary fishing pools show only ripples; only deep pools keep the gold light marker. Farm plot rows follow the slope of the ground.
The Caged Scout sits in a real cage whose door swings open when you free them. The chain coif covers the top of your head. The Pail and Plough has one well again.
Resetting talents or perks at the Unbinder costs a share of what a character of your level really earns (about 500 gold at level 9).

entries.title: Clearer profession lessons
items: The prospector now clearly confirms that you have learned Mining and received a pick. His Mining button stays available on later visits, with your skill, tool and mining instructions.
Other profession teachers also show whether you already know their trades and keep their training details available.

entries.title: Profession trainers in every major town
items: Every major town now has dedicated Mining, Logging, Foraging and Skinning trainers, alongside its crafting teachers. Lessons and your first gathering tool are free.
Search the map for a profession, such as mining or foraging, to find its teachers. Gathering trainers also have their own map filters.
Bram Delver now appears on the map as a Mining trainer at Torborhold's main gate.

entries.title: Better phone controls, steady auto-attack and party tracking
items: Tap Attack to pick an enemy, move into reach and keep attacking. Tap again to stop; moving by hand keeps auto-attack on.
Phones now have named Fish and Mount buttons, useful button labels, and a guide to the controls. Fishing rods no longer occupy potion slots.
Profession mini-games wait for your first input before starting, or begin after six seconds. Starting an activity releases held movement.
Party members off screen have direction arrows. Hold a party portrait to track someone.
The map controls wrap on phones, and the game view follows changes to the size of the screen.
Saved characters show their equipped gear on the title screen. Class resources such as Starlight now update on your character frame.
Fixed scrolling lists and update notices covering the game. Silver ore sells for slightly more to keep mining income in line with other activities.

entries.title: Professions, phone play, guards and thirty fixes from your reports
items: Added ten professions: mine ore boulders, fell marked trees, forage and skin, then smelt, forge, stitch, brew, cook and temper at the town's trade buildings — each a quick mini-game. Start with Bram Delver just inside Torborhold's main gate.
Phone support: on a phone the game now switches to a touch layout by itself — thumb stick, skill arcs, a quick wheel and full-screen menus. Controllers work too.
Town guards now stand at every gate and square and fight raiders first, and no raid or nearby event starts while a character under level 3 or in their first ten minutes is there.
Enemy archers and casters now fire arrows and bolts you can see flying from them, and the damage lands when the shot does.
Horses were rebuilt with an arched neck, a proper head with small set-in eyes, real ears and jointed legs; all mounts use the new body.
Monsters in the first levels give half again as much experience, and quest hand-ins were raised to match.
Ox carts by each town's main gate take you to any other town for a small fare; a carter in Orrinsford gives your first ride free.
Every town's gates now open onto a proper main street that runs clear to the town square — Torborhold's three gates included.
A report sent by an admin is approved automatically.
In the loot window, E takes the selected item and F takes everything.
Unread mail now shows only the yellow dot on the Party button.
The account was linked; the refusal was a level-5 rule applied to the new character. It now looks at your highest character and says exactly what is missing.
Quest givers show a gold "!" and hand-ins a gold "?" above their heads and on the map (grey when not yet available).
You can hide an event with the crossed-eye button on its card and bring it back from the line under the events or the map's Events list.
Firebolt and every other bolt, arrow and thrown attack now travels to its target and deals its damage on arrival.
The map opens where you left it, and a filter and search box find stables, anglers, trainers and other services, ringing the towns that have them.
The minimap's own "click for the map" tooltip is gone, so pin tooltips are no longer covered.
Quest zones on the map and minimap light up under the pointer and show the quest and its objective.
Distant hills and mountains are now covered in trees up to the tree line.
Backpacks can be worn on the back instead of a cloak: fewer bonuses, but 4, 6 or 8 extra bag slots. The tailor sells them.
You now run by default; hold Shift to walk, and Num Lock toggles auto-run.
A damage meter is available under Settings → Game → "Damage meter" (off by default; /meter also toggles it).
Lanterns and torches are removed and refunded in gold; everyone carries a wider light and dungeons have ambient light.
Starting equipment is now 4–6 clearly different choices per class, each labelled with how it plays, and the three armour sets give different bonuses.
Event chests stay until everyone has looted or two minutes pass, are locked only by their own named keepers, and can no longer be emptied by looting a nearby corpse.
An item's icon is now drawn from the same model your character wears; the War Helm looks like a war helm in both places.
Calling your mount makes you stand still until it arrives (press again to cancel), then you carry on the way you were going.
Only NPCs who offer a shop, service or quest show a title above their name.
Feedback has a "My reports" tab showing each report's state and how it was resolved, and you can reply to a report.

entries.title: Your first bug reports, an economy overhaul and more fishing
items: Starting equipment now offers 4–6 clearly different packs per class; every pack fills both hands or is a two-hander, and shield classes always have a weapon-and-shield pack.
The minimap now shows enemies, people, doors, stairs and chests in your line of sight, in dungeons too.
The +6 armour perk was applied but the tooltip was stale; damage reduction is armour ÷ (100 + armour), shown to one decimal, and the perk is now +10.
Dying in a dungeon puts you back at the start of the floor you died on, and the stair up lets you pick a floor when there is more than one above.
Healers could not heal at levels 1–2 because the heal unlocked at level 3; every healing class now has its direct heal from level 1, and clicking a party frame targets that member.
A dungeon now has exactly one way out, behind the last boss; the door by the entrance is labelled "The way you came in".
Druids have a wolf form, Moonpelt Shape, with a Wolf Pack talent that calls two wolf companions.
Event result cards no longer print "null"; every result now carries a real sentence.
The raid boss at Torborhold had borrowed a dungeon boss's script, including a ward only braziers could break; he now has his own script with no ward.
Every boss ward now has a stated duration, breaks under enough damage, and shows a bar with the time left.
The bag window's armour and damage now come from the same numbers as the Character menu.
Shields really did give 0.2% block; they now give 20% and say so, and existing shields were corrected.
Potions and other consumables stack up to 20; Shift-click splits a stack and dropping one on another joins them.
That was an oat field drawn as pale boxes; grain is now drawn as standing stalks.
Danger zones and telegraphs now end the moment their caster dies or is interrupted.
Healing potions now restore 50% of your health (greater: 80%) on a 20-second cooldown, and drop from monsters.
Shapeshift skills now change your character's model into the shape.
Gold and prices were reworked: an hour of play buys about one uncommon upgrade, a rare takes a few hours, and fishing is a real way to earn — with prized fish, legend fish and sunken crates.
385 fishing pools now sit along rivers, lakes and the coast, with one near almost every town.
Characters who reach level 3 get a letter inviting feedback; your first report earns a gift.

entries.title: Angling, starting equipment, revives and a new look at events
items: Angling: cast a line at any water, tug the catch in, fill a catch journal and cook at a campfire.
A starting-equipment step in character creation: pick an armour set and a weapon pack.
Events now say what is happening, what to do, how long is left and what you earn — and they end properly.
Rare and champion monsters are far more common.
Priest, cleric, druid, paladin, necromancer and shaman each have their own revive; every healing class has a direct heal on key 1 or 2.
A Character menu (V) with stats and ability damage that sits beside the bag.
A Feedback button: send a suggestion or a bug report from inside the game.
66 new pieces of gear, new wand, staff and focus attack styles, and dual-wield attack animations.
Perk and talent picks are staged with Undo, Redo and Accept — nothing is spent until you accept.
Town buildings are taller, gates sit properly in their walls, and fences face the right way.
